BE-ERR-001.title: Centralized AppError Exception Hierarchy
BE-ERR-001.statement: Application errors must instantiate or subclass AppError, encapsulating HTTP statusCode, a machine-readable errorCode, and a safe client message.
BE-ERR-001.book_title: Design and Build Great Web APIs
BE-ERR-001.evidence_quote: Errors should be treated as first-class citizens. Creating structured error representations with HTTP status codes makes debugging predictable.

BE-ERR-002.title: Never Expose Internal Stack Traces in Production
BE-ERR-002.statement: Production error responses must never expose raw stack traces, SQL queries, database column names, or internal file system paths.
BE-ERR-002.evidence_quote: Stack traces and internal system details must never be returned to the client in production. They provide adversaries with valuable reconnaissance information.

BE-API-002.title: Uniform API Response Envelope
BE-API-002.statement: All API endpoints must return a standardized JSON envelope with consistent success and error schemas.
BE-API-002.evidence_quote: A consistent response envelope ensures that clients reliably distinguish between data payloads and error payloads, preventing parsing ambiguities and unintended data leakage.

BE-API-001.title: RESTful Plural Nouns and Kebab-Case Endpoints
BE-API-001.statement: REST API URI paths must use plural nouns in kebab-case for resource collections and avoid verbs in URI paths.
BE-API-001.book_title: Design and Build Great Web APIs
BE-API-001.evidence_quote: URIs identify resources, not actions. By convention, resource collections are named with plural nouns to represent sets of entities, and HTTP verbs operate on those resources.

BE-VAL-001.title: Boundary Request Validation via Zod Schemas
BE-VAL-001.statement: All incoming HTTP requests (body, query, params) must be validated by Zod schemas in middleware before touching controller logic.
BE-VAL-001.evidence_quote: Validation must occur at the boundary of the API. Any input that does not conform to the strict schema must be rejected immediately before processing.

BE-VAL-002.title: Strict Rejection of Unknown Request Fields
BE-VAL-002.statement: Validation schemas must strip or strictly reject unrecognized fields to prevent mass assignment vulnerabilities.
BE-VAL-002.evidence_quote: Mass assignment occurs when a client binds HTTP request parameters directly into data objects. Strict schemas must disallow unexpected properties.

BE-IDEM-001.title: Active Idempotency Deduplication Execution
BE-IDEM-001.statement: Endpoints receiving mutation requests with an Idempotency-Key must actively query for existing records using fast-path caching or double-checked locking inside database transactions, returning the cached result (HTTP 200) instead of re-executing mutations. Validating and storing the key without duplicate querying is strictly forbidden as decorative security.
BE-IDEM-001.book_title: Design and Build Great Web APIs
BE-IDEM-001.evidence_quote: An idempotency key allows clients to safely retry requests without fear of performing the same operation twice. The server must check for the presence of the key in prior transactions before executing state modifications.

ARCH-DDD-001.title: Explicit Definition of Bounded Contexts
ARCH-DDD-001.statement: Each subsystem must maintain an explicit Bounded Context with its own Ubiquitous Language; domain models must not be shared indiscriminately across contexts.
ARCH-DDD-001.evidence_quote: A bounded context is a boundary within a domain where a particular domain model applies... dividing a system into bounded contexts protects against model pollution.

ARCH-DDD-002.title: Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) for External Services
ARCH-DDD-002.statement: Third-party APIs (e.g. Gemini, DeepSeek, S3) must be isolated behind an Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) that translates vendor payloads into internal domain models.
ARCH-DDD-002.evidence_quote: An anti-corruption layer translates between two bounded contexts or an external system, preventing foreign concepts and models from polluting the internal model.

ARCH-DDD-003.title: Aggregate Root Invariant Encapsulation and Transactional Boundary
ARCH-DDD-003.statement: Domain mutations must be executed strictly through the Aggregate Root entity; external code must never directly alter the state of child entities within an aggregate boundary.
ARCH-DDD-003.section: The Aggregate Pattern and Invariant Protection
ARCH-DDD-003.evidence_quote: An Aggregate is an explicit boundary around a cluster of entities and value objects. All modifications must enter through the Aggregate Root to protect consistency invariants.

ARCH-DDD-004.title: Domain Events and Transactional Outbox for Asynchronous Decoupling
ARCH-DDD-004.statement: Cross-subsystem side effects (e.g. triggering embedding, vector indexing, email notifications) must be emitted as Domain Events and committed via the Transactional Outbox pattern within the same database transaction.
ARCH-DDD-004.section: The Outbox Pattern for Reliable Messaging
ARCH-DDD-004.evidence_quote: To avoid dual-write inconsistencies when publishing domain events, commit the event to an outbox table within the same database transaction as the entity state.

ARCH-LAY-001.title: Strict Enforcement of Layer Isolation (No Layer Skipping)
ARCH-LAY-001.statement: Requests must flow strictly through defined architectural layers: Route -> Controller -> Service -> Repository/Prisma. Upper layers must not bypass intermediate layers.
ARCH-LAY-001.evidence_quote: Layers of isolation means that changes made in one layer of the architecture generally do not ripple through to other layers... closed layers enforce this boundary.

ARCH-SINK-001.title: Avoid Architecture Sinkhole Anti-Pattern
ARCH-SINK-001.statement: Do not construct redundant pass-through layers that perform no calculation, validation, transformation, or orchestration.
ARCH-SINK-001.evidence_quote: The architecture sinkhole anti-pattern occurs when requests flow through multiple layers of the architecture as simple pass-through processing with little or no logic performed within each layer.

ARCH-MOD-001.title: High Cohesion within Domain Modules
ARCH-MOD-001.statement: Modules must exhibit high functional cohesion, where all classes, services, and schemas within a module contribute directly to a single well-defined business domain.
ARCH-MOD-001.evidence_quote: Cohesion refers to what extent the parts of a module should be contained within the same module. High cohesion means elements are strongly related and focused on a single task.

ARCH-MOD-002.title: Low Coupling and Explicit Module Contracts
ARCH-MOD-002.statement: Inter-module dependencies must be strictly decoupled and accessed exclusively through exported public service interfaces or event contracts, never reaching into internal sub-paths.
ARCH-MOD-002.evidence_quote: Coupling measures the degree of interdependence between software modules; low coupling represents a good design that supports high maintainability.

ARCH-MOD-003.title: Eliminate Connascence of Execution Order
ARCH-MOD-003.statement: Public service methods must not require external callers to invoke separate methods in an undocumented chronological sequence to produce a valid domain state.
ARCH-MOD-003.evidence_quote: Connascence of Execution occurs when the order of execution between multiple components matters. Architects should strive to minimize non-local connascence.

ARCH-MONO-001.title: Modular Monolith Domain-Driven Partitioning
ARCH-MONO-001.statement: Monolithic backends must partition code by domain/feature boundaries rather than technical layers, encapsulating data schemas, logic, and endpoints together.
ARCH-MONO-001.evidence_quote: The modular monolith architecture style emphasizes domain partitioning... components are grouped by business domains rather than technical capabilities.

BE-DB-001.title: Mandatory Tenant and User Scoping on Database Queries
BE-DB-001.statement: Every database query retrieving or mutating user-owned resources must include an explicit WHERE userId = :currentUserId or orgId filter.
BE-DB-001.evidence_quote: Access control checks must ensure that the user requesting the resource has legitimate ownership. Scoping queries by user ID prevents unauthorized object access.

BE-DB-002.title: Atomic Transactions for Multi-Table Writes
BE-DB-002.statement: All database write operations affecting multiple tables or cascading dependencies must be encapsulated within an atomic transaction.
BE-DB-002.evidence_quote: Transactions provide atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability. Operations that span multiple entities must execute within a unified transactional boundary.

RAG-CHK-001.title: Deterministic Word Window Chunking with Overlap
RAG-CHK-001.statement: Document text must be chunked into deterministic word windows (500 words) with a mandatory boundary overlap (50 words).
RAG-CHK-001.evidence_quote: Boundary overlap ensures that contextual information spanning chunk boundaries is preserved. A 10% overlap is standard for general prose.

RAG-CIT-001.title: Verifiable Source Grounding and Citation Metadata
RAG-CIT-001.statement: Every retrieved chunk injected into the LLM context must carry immutable provenance metadata (documentId, documentTitle, pageNumber, sheetName).
RAG-CIT-001.evidence_quote: Preserving chunk provenance from extraction through generation is essential for grounded citations, giving users the confidence to verify generated answers.

RAG-PRM-001.title: Strict Contextual Framing and Anti-Hallucination Prompting
RAG-PRM-001.statement: System instructions must explicitly instruct the LLM to answer strictly using the provided context, and to state clearly that information is missing if the context is insufficient.
RAG-PRM-001.evidence_quote: Prompt framing must establish strict epistemic boundaries: the model must be explicitly forbidden from drawing on outside knowledge when answering document queries.

RAG-ASY-001.title: Asynchronous Background Processing for Multi-Page Document Ingestion
RAG-ASY-001.statement: Documents exceeding 5MB or 20 pages must be ingested asynchronously via background worker jobs, returning an immediate 202 Accepted status with a job status tracking endpoint.
RAG-ASY-001.evidence_quote: Large document ingestion must be decoupled from the synchronous HTTP request-response cycle. Use background workers to extract, chunk, and embed documents asynchronously.

RAG-EVL-001.title: Automated Groundedness and Faithfulness Evaluation
RAG-EVL-001.statement: RAG generation quality must be continuously audited against a golden evaluation dataset measuring Faithfulness (answer grounded in context) and Answer Relevance.
RAG-EVL-001.evidence_quote: Evaluating a RAG application requires measuring the RAG triad: context relevance, groundedness (faithfulness), and answer relevance against curated ground truth.

RAG-VEC-001.title: Normalized High-Dimensional Cosine Similarity Search
RAG-VEC-001.statement: pgvector similarity search must compute Cosine Distance (<=> operator) against normalized 3,072-dimensional embedding vectors.
RAG-VEC-001.evidence_quote: Cosine similarity is the preferred distance metric for semantic text embeddings as it evaluates the cosine of the angle between vectors, normalizing for document length.

SEC-AUTH-001.title: Dual-Token Architecture (15m Memory Access + 7d HttpOnly Cookie Refresh)
SEC-AUTH-001.statement: JWT access tokens must have a short lifespan (<= 15 minutes) kept in memory, while refresh tokens (7 days) must be stored in an httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookie.
SEC-AUTH-001.book_title: Alice and Bob Learn Application Security
SEC-AUTH-001.evidence_quote: Cookies containing session tokens must always have the httpOnly flag set to protect them from XSS theft, and the Secure flag to ensure transmission over HTTPS only.

SEC-AUTH-002.title: Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) for Sensitive Administrative Operations
SEC-AUTH-002.statement: Security-sensitive operations (password reset, email change, organization deletion, API key generation) must require step-up MFA verification.
SEC-AUTH-002.book_title: Alice and Bob Learn Application Security
SEC-AUTH-002.evidence_quote: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) requires two or more distinct verification factors, significantly reducing the risk of unauthorized account takeovers.

SEC-AUTH-003.title: Mandatory Role and Permission Enforcement at Route Boundaries (Anti-BFLA)
SEC-AUTH-003.statement: Every sensitive, administrative, or group-level endpoint must verify that the authenticated user possesses the specific required role or permission before invoking business logic.
SEC-AUTH-003.evidence_quote: Function level authorization requires verifying that the user not only is logged in, but also holds explicit rights to execute the targeted operation.

SEC-JWT-001.title: Strict Verification of JWT Issuer, Audience, Expiry, and Algorithm
SEC-JWT-001.statement: JWT token verification must strictly enforce algorithm white-listing (rejecting 'none'), and validate 'iss' (issuer), 'aud' (audience), and 'exp' (expiration) claims.
SEC-JWT-001.evidence_quote: Always specify the expected signature algorithms explicitly and validate all registered claims (iss, aud, exp) to prevent token spoofing and replay.

SEC-UPL-001.title: Magic Bytes File Signature Verification on Uploads
SEC-UPL-001.statement: Uploaded files must be verified by reading their initial magic byte signatures, never relying solely on the client-supplied MIME type or file extension.
SEC-UPL-001.book_title: Alice and Bob Learn Application Security
SEC-UPL-001.evidence_quote: Never trust the client-provided Content-Type or file extension. Verify the actual file content using magic bytes to ensure it matches the expected format.

SEC-UPL-002.title: Strict File Size Limits and Memory Quotas
SEC-UPL-002.statement: File upload endpoints must enforce a strict maximum file size limit (20MB) and total payload quota to prevent Denial of Service (DoS).
SEC-UPL-002.book_title: Alice and Bob Learn Application Security
SEC-UPL-002.section: Denial of Service via File Uploads
SEC-UPL-002.evidence_quote: Enforce strict size limits on uploaded files at the reverse proxy and application level to protect against memory exhaustion and storage starvation.

SEC-SSRF-001.title: Strict URL Validation and Private IP Filtering (Anti-SSRF)
SEC-SSRF-001.statement: Any API endpoint accepting a remote URL (e.g., document ingestion, webhook) must strictly validate the protocol (http/https only), resolve DNS, and block all private, loopback, link-local, and cloud metadata IP ranges before initiating an outbound request.
SEC-SSRF-001.evidence_quote: Never trust a client-supplied URL without resolving its IP and ensuring it does not target local network interfaces or internal cloud metadata addresses.

SEC-RAT-001.title: Strict Rate Limiting on Authentication and AI Generation Endpoints
SEC-RAT-001.statement: Sensitive endpoints (login, password reset, file ingestion, AI LLM generation) must enforce rate limiting per IP and authenticated user identifier to prevent brute-force attacks, resource exhaustion, and Denial of Service.
SEC-RAT-001.evidence_quote: Rate limiting is a primary defense against automated brute-force attacks. Every authentication and computationally heavy endpoint must impose strict threshold limits.

SEC-LOG-001.title: Automated PII and Credential Masking in Structured Logs
SEC-LOG-001.statement: Structured loggers must automatically sanitize and mask passwords, JWT tokens, API keys, credit cards, and personal identifiable information (PII).
SEC-LOG-001.book_title: Alice and Bob Learn Application Security
SEC-LOG-001.evidence_quote: Never log sensitive data such as passwords, session tokens, personal identifiable information (PII), or private encryption keys.

SEC-AI-001.title: Isolation and Demarcation Against Prompt Injections
SEC-AI-001.statement: Retrieved document text must be treated as untrusted user data and enclosed within explicit cryptographic or semantic boundary tags (e.g. <context>...</context>).
SEC-AI-001.evidence_quote: Treat all retrieved content as untrusted input. Demarcate external data using clear boundary tags and instruct the model to treat content inside tags as passive data.

SEC-AI-002.title: Output Sanitization of LLM Generated Content
SEC-AI-002.statement: All Markdown and HTML responses generated by the LLM must be sanitized using DOMPurify before rendering into the client DOM.
SEC-AI-002.evidence_quote: LLM output cannot be considered safe. Always pass generated markdown through a robust HTML sanitizer before rendering in web browsers.

SEC-AI-003.title: Least-Privilege Execution and Confirmation for Tool-Calling Agents
SEC-AI-003.statement: AI Agents and MCP tool runners must operate with least-privilege permissions; tools that mutate database records, send external emails, or delete resources must require explicit user approval.
SEC-AI-003.evidence_quote: Apply least privilege to AI tools and agents. Any action that modifies data or causes external side effects should require explicit human confirmation.

TEST-INT-001.title: Integration Tests with Real Database State Rollback
TEST-INT-001.statement: Integration tests must execute against a real PostgreSQL instance with pgvector enabled, rolling back transactions after each test to ensure state cleanliness.
TEST-INT-001.book_title: Unit Testing Principles, Practices, and Patterns
TEST-INT-001.evidence_quote: Do not mock the database in integration tests. An integration test that uses a mock database is not an integration test; verify queries against a real instance.

TEST-MCK-001.title: Restrict Mocking to Out-of-Process Unmanaged Dependencies
TEST-MCK-001.statement: Only mock external, out-of-process unmanaged dependencies that you do not own (e.g., Gemini API, DeepSeek API, Nodemailer). Do not mock internal classes, helpers, or managed databases.
TEST-MCK-001.book_title: Unit Testing Principles, Practices, and Patterns
TEST-MCK-001.evidence_quote: Mock only unmanaged dependencies—dependencies with which you communicate through external APIs that you do not control. Never mock internal domain classes or managed dependencies.

TEST-MCK-002.title: Verify State and Output, Never Interaction Counts on Internals
TEST-MCK-002.statement: Tests must not assert internal method invocation counts (e.g. expect(internalHelper).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)) on internal components.
TEST-MCK-002.book_title: Unit Testing Principles, Practices, and Patterns
TEST-MCK-002.evidence_quote: Verifying internal interactions leaks implementation details into tests. Tests should verify observable behavior: the output values and resulting state changes.

TEST-DBL-001.title: Strict Test Double Taxonomy: Prefer Fakes and Stubs Over Interaction Mocks
TEST-DBL-001.statement: Test suites must distinguish between Fakes (lightweight in-memory implementations), Stubs (canned queries), and Mocks (interaction verification). Prefer Fakes and Stubs over brittle interaction Mocks.
TEST-DBL-001.section: Fakes, Stubs, and Mocks in Practice
TEST-DBL-001.evidence_quote: Prefer real implementations or in-memory fakes over mocks. Mocks often lead to brittle tests that break on refactoring without finding real bugs.

TEST-PIL-001.title: The Four Pillars of Unit Test Quality
TEST-PIL-001.statement: Every unit test must maximize Protection Against Regressions, Resistance to Refactoring, Fast Feedback, and Maintainability.
TEST-PIL-001.book_title: Unit Testing Principles, Practices, and Patterns
TEST-PIL-001.evidence_quote: A good unit test has four foundational attributes: protection against regressions, resistance to refactoring, fast feedback, and maintainability. Resistance to refactoring is non-negotiable.

TEST-AAA-001.title: Standardized Arrange-Act-Assert (AAA) Test Structure
TEST-AAA-001.statement: Every test case must follow the Arrange-Act-Assert (AAA) pattern with clearly separated phases, containing only a single Act invocation.
TEST-AAA-001.book_title: Unit Testing Principles, Practices, and Patterns
TEST-AAA-001.evidence_quote: The AAA pattern provides a uniform structure across all tests in a test suite. It splits a test into three sections: Arrange, Act, and Assert.

TEST-ANT-001.title: Unit Testing Anti-Patterns: Never Test Private Methods or Mock Concrete Classes
TEST-ANT-001.statement: Unit tests must only verify observable public behavior; tests must never inspect or invoke private methods, expose internal state for testing, or mock concrete business classes.
TEST-ANT-001.book_title: Unit Testing Principles, Practices, and Patterns
TEST-ANT-001.section: Testing Private Methods and Leaking Domain Knowledge
TEST-ANT-001.evidence_quote: Do not test private methods directly. Private methods are implementation details. Testing them binds tests to the code structure and hurts maintainability.

SWE-STY-001.title: Automated Formatting and Style Guides as Common Law
SWE-STY-001.statement: Code formatting must be entirely delegated to automated deterministic tools (Prettier, ESLint). Style debates must never take place in manual code reviews.
SWE-STY-001.evidence_quote: The goal of a style guide is to produce consistency across the codebase. Enforce rules automatically using formatters and linters so humans can focus on design.

CODE-FUN-001.title: Single Responsibility Principle (SRP) for Functions
CODE-FUN-001.statement: Every function and method must perform a single, well-defined task and operate at a consistent level of abstraction.
CODE-FUN-001.book_title: Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship
CODE-FUN-001.evidence_quote: Functions should do one thing. They should do it well. They should do it only. If a function does only those steps that are one level below the stated name, it does one thing.

CODE-FUN-002.title: Small Function Size and Guard Clause Early Returns
CODE-FUN-002.statement: Functions should not exceed 40 lines of logic and must use guard clauses (early returns) to maintain a cyclomatic nesting depth of 3 or less.
CODE-FUN-002.book_title: Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship
CODE-FUN-002.evidence_quote: Functions should hardly ever be 20 lines long... the indent level of a function should not be greater than one or two.
CODE-FUN-002.adaptation_note: Clean Code Chapter 3 recommends functions rarely exceeding 20 lines. Kantanda purposefully extends this limit to 40 lines to pragmatically accommodate TypeScript parameter types, asynchronous await sequences, and robust error branching without excessive function fragmentation.

CODE-DEM-001.title: Law of Demeter (Principle of Least Knowledge)
CODE-DEM-001.statement: A method must only invoke methods on: (1) its own object, (2) objects passed in as arguments, (3) objects it instantiates, and (4) its direct collaborators. Deep chaining of accessors is strictly forbidden.
CODE-DEM-001.book_title: Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship
CODE-DEM-001.evidence_quote: A module should not know about the innards of the objects it manipulates. A method f of a class C should only call the methods of C, objects created by f, or objects passed as arguments to f.

CODE-DES-001.title: Kent Beck's Four Rules of Simple Design
CODE-DES-001.statement: During code construction and refactoring, design choices must adhere to the four rules of simple design in strict priority order: 1. Runs all tests, 2. Contains no duplication, 3. Expresses intent clearly, 4. Minimizes elements.
CODE-DES-001.book_title: Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship
CODE-DES-001.section: The Four Rules of Simple Design
CODE-DES-001.evidence_quote: According to Kent Beck, a design is 'simple' if it follows these rules: Runs all the tests; Contains no duplication; Expresses the intent of the programmer; Minimizes the number of classes and methods.

CODE-NAM-001.title: Intent-Revealing, Searchable Identifiers
CODE-NAM-001.statement: Variable and function names must clearly express their intent, domain concept, and unit of measurement without requiring external comments.
CODE-NAM-001.book_title: Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship
CODE-NAM-001.evidence_quote: The name of a variable, function, or class, should answer all the big questions. It should tell you why it exists, what it does, and how it is used.

ARCH-ADR-001.title: Mandatory Architectural Decision Records (ADR) for Structural Decisions
ARCH-ADR-001.statement: Any structural architectural decision that introduces new database engines, external protocols, communication patterns, or alters boundary contracts must be documented in a committed Architectural Decision Record (ADR).
ARCH-ADR-001.evidence_quote: An Architectural Decision Record (ADR) captures an important architectural decision made along with its context and consequences. It provides lasting documentation of architectural intent.

CODE-DOC-001.title: Comments Must Explain 'Why', Never 'What'
CODE-DOC-001.statement: In-line comments must explain technical rationale, non-obvious business requirements, or architectural trade-offs; they must never simply narrate the code.
CODE-DOC-001.book_title: Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship
CODE-DOC-001.evidence_quote: Comments do not make up for bad code. Clear and expressive code with few comments is far superior to a cluttered and complex code with lots of comments.

CODE-DOC-002.title: Comprehensive TSDoc on Public Services and Interfaces
CODE-DOC-002.statement: All exported services, utilities, and API client methods must have formal TSDoc comments with @param, @returns, and @throws tags.
CODE-DOC-002.evidence_quote: Document the interfaces, not the implementation. Good API documentation describes pre-conditions, post-conditions, parameters, and failure modes.

SWE-REV-001.title: Five-Point Code Review Verification Checklist
SWE-REV-001.statement: Every Pull Request must be audited against 5 criteria before approval: Correctness, Security, Architecture Alignment, Test Coverage, and Readability.
SWE-REV-001.evidence_quote: Code review evaluates design, functionality, complexity, tests, naming, comments, and style. The reviewer should ensure the code improves the codebase overall.

GIT-CMT-001.title: Conventional Commits v1.0.0 Specification
GIT-CMT-001.statement: Git commit messages must strictly adhere to the Conventional Commits specification: <type>(<scope>): <short description> in lowercase.
GIT-CMT-001.evidence_quote: Meaningful, structured commit messages enable automated traceability between requirements, source code modifications, and release artifacts.

CD-GAT-001.title: Automated Pre-Commit and CI Quality Gates
CD-GAT-001.statement: Git commits and CI builds must enforce automated quality gates: ESLint (zero errors), TypeScript type-check (tsc --noEmit), and automated unit tests.
CD-GAT-001.evidence_quote: The commit stage should run fast automated unit tests, linting, and compile checks. If any check fails, the build fails immediately, giving instant feedback.

SWE-DEP-001.title: Deterministic Dependency Pinning and Vulnerability Auditing
SWE-DEP-001.statement: Package dependencies must be strictly committed with lockfiles (package-lock.json). CI must execute npm audit / security vulnerability scans on every build.
SWE-DEP-001.evidence_quote: Dependencies represent an ongoing commitment and risk. Pin exact dependency versions and automate security audits to protect against supply chain vulnerabilities.

SWE-TST-001.title: Hermetic Test Isolation and Explicit Test Sizing
SWE-TST-001.statement: Tests must be explicitly categorized by size (Small/Unit, Medium/Integration, Large/E2E). Small tests must be hermetic, running in-memory with zero disk, network, or external process access.
SWE-TST-001.evidence_quote: Google classifies tests as Small, Medium, and Large. Small tests must be hermetic: no access to network or disk. Hermetic tests are fast, reliable, and deterministic.

TEST-TRUTH-001.title: Truth-in-Testing: Prohibition of False Concurrency Claims on In-Memory Fakes
TEST-TRUTH-001.statement: Pull requests and walkthrough documentation must never claim concurrency locking or race-condition verification based solely on in-memory fake repositories. If a test runs on an in-memory double without real engine locks, the report must state that runtime concurrency is unverified.
TEST-TRUTH-001.book_title: Unit Testing Principles, Practices, and Patterns
TEST-TRUTH-001.evidence_quote: Faking or mocking out the database in integration tests is an anti-pattern. You must test against the real database engine because in-memory mocks do not replicate transactional and concurrency semantics.

TEST-RACE-001.title: Mandatory Concurrent Execution Testing for Concurrency and Locking Claims
TEST-RACE-001.statement: Any code asserting race-condition prevention, optimistic locking, or pessimistic locking must include at least one automated test executing N concurrent requests via Promise.all asserting exact fulfilled/rejected counts and balance invariant preservation.
TEST-RACE-001.evidence_quote: Transactional concurrency mechanisms must be validated with simulated concurrent load tests that deliberately induce conflict and assert invariant preservation.

TEST-IDEM-001.title: Mandatory Behavioral Idempotency Deduplication Testing
TEST-IDEM-001.statement: Any endpoint or service accepting an Idempotency-Key must include at least one automated test executing two consecutive requests with the identical key, asserting that the second call returns the original result without secondary balance or state mutations.
TEST-IDEM-001.book_title: Unit Testing Principles, Practices, and Patterns
TEST-IDEM-001.evidence_quote: Tests must verify observable business behavior, not implementation details. For idempotent endpoints, the observable behavior is that multiple identical requests produce the exact same system state as a single request.

DS-BTN-001.title: Button Loading State and Disabled Accessibility
DS-BTN-001.statement: While an asynchronous action is executing, buttons must display an inline spinner, maintain their exact layout width to prevent content reflow, and have aria-busy='true' and disabled attributes set.
DS-BTN-001.book_title: Design System Specifications / Laws of UX

DS-BTN-002.title: Minimum 48x48px Touch Target
DS-BTN-002.statement: All interactive buttons on mobile and desktop viewports must maintain a touch/click target of at least 48x48px per Fitts's Law (UI-LAW-002).
DS-BTN-002.book_title: Design System Specifications / Laws of UX

DS-BTN-003.title: Single Primary Button Per Visual Area
DS-BTN-003.statement: Each view or modal card must present at most one primary solid-color call-to-action button to eliminate visual competition and cognitive friction.
DS-BTN-003.book_title: Design System Specifications / Laws of UX

DS-DLG-001.title: Destructive Dialog Typing
DS-DLG-001.statement: Destructive actions (delete, reset) must require typing resource name or explicit 2-step confirmation (UI-DLG-001).
DS-DLG-001.book_title: Design System Specifications / Laws of UX

DS-DLG-002.title: Focus Trap & Escape Close
DS-DLG-002.statement: Modals must trap focus internally and close on Escape key press (UI-DLG-002).
DS-DLG-002.book_title: Design System Specifications / Laws of UX

DS-DLG-003.title: Touch Target Size
DS-DLG-003.statement: All clickable buttons inside dialogs must have a minimum touch target of 48x48px (UI-LAW-002).
DS-DLG-003.book_title: Design System Specifications / Laws of UX

DS-INP-001.title: Explicit Label and Accessible Error Association
DS-INP-001.statement: Every form input must be linked to an explicit <label htmlFor={id}> and point to its validation error message via aria-describedby when invalid.
DS-INP-001.book_title: Design System Specifications / Laws of UX

DS-INP-002.title: Persistent Focus Rings
DS-INP-002.statement: Input focus rings must never be removed with outline-none without replacing with an accessible high-contrast focus ring (e.g. ring-2 ring-indigo-500).
DS-INP-002.book_title: Design System Specifications / Laws of UX

DS-TBL-001.title: Virtualization for Datasets Exceeding 100 Rows
DS-TBL-001.statement: Tables or document lists displaying more than 100 entries must implement windowed virtualization via TanStack Virtual to cap DOM node count and preserve 60 FPS scrolling.
DS-TBL-001.book_title: Design System Specifications / Laws of UX

DS-TBL-002.title: Empty and Zero-Search States
DS-TBL-002.statement: Tables must render dedicated EmptyState graphics and actionable reset filters when row collections are empty or search results return zero items.
DS-TBL-002.book_title: Design System Specifications / Laws of UX

DS-TST-001.title: Accessible Toast Notifications with Polite Live Regions
DS-TST-001.statement: Non-critical status notifications must use aria-live='polite' and role='status'; critical errors must use role='alert'. Auto-dismissing toasts must pause on hover and keyboard focus.
DS-TST-001.book_title: Design System Specifications / Laws of UX

FE-ARCH-002.title: Colocation of Feature Components and Hooks
FE-ARCH-002.statement: Components, hooks, api callers, and types specific to a single feature must be colocated under src/features/<feature>/ rather than scattered into global directories.
FE-ARCH-002.evidence_quote: Colocating components, hooks, and types by feature keeps dependencies localized and simplifies long-term maintenance.

FE-ARCH-001.title: Server-First Components in Next.js App Router
FE-ARCH-001.statement: React components in the Next.js App Router must be React Server Components (RSC) by default. The 'use client' directive must only be applied at leaf interactive components.
FE-ARCH-001.evidence_quote: Default to Server Components to reduce bundle size and leverage streaming. Push the 'use client' boundary down to the leaves of your component tree.

FE-API-001.title: Decoupled API Client Service Layer (No Fetch/Axios in JSX)
FE-API-001.statement: UI components must not call axios or fetch directly in JSX event handlers or useEffect hooks; all calls must be encapsulated in typed API service functions.
FE-API-001.book_title: Learn React with TypeScript - Third Edition
FE-API-001.evidence_quote: Encapsulate HTTP requests in dedicated API modules. Components should consume strongly-typed functions rather than interacting with the network client directly.

FE-FRM-001.title: React Hook Form Combined with Zod Schema Resolver
FE-FRM-001.statement: All forms must be managed with React Hook Form and validated against a shared Zod schema using @hookform/resolvers/zod.
FE-FRM-001.book_title: Learn React with TypeScript - Third Edition
FE-FRM-001.evidence_quote: Using React Hook Form with Zod schemas ensures type-safe forms with minimal re-renders and aligns frontend validation directly with backend contracts.

FE-ACT-001.title: Server Actions Mutation Lifecycle with useActionState and useOptimistic
FE-ACT-001.statement: Mutations executed via Next.js Server Actions must be managed in the UI using React 19's useActionState and useOptimistic to provide immediate user feedback and progressive enhancement.
FE-ACT-001.evidence_quote: Server Actions combined with useActionState streamline form lifecycles, enabling type-safe server validation and optimistic state updates with zero boilerplate.

FE-STA-001.title: Strict State Separation (Server vs Global UI vs Form State)
FE-STA-001.statement: Frontend state must be strictly partitioned into Server State (caching API data), Global UI State (Zustand: active modal, sidebar), and Form State (React Hook Form).
FE-STA-001.book_title: Learn React with TypeScript - Third Edition
FE-STA-001.evidence_quote: Partition state into server state and client state. Do not manage server data in client global state managers without dedicated caching semantics.

FE-STA-002.title: URL-as-State for Search Queries, Filters, and Pagination
FE-STA-002.statement: State that alters the primary view of data (search terms, filter categories, sorting order, active pagination page) must be synchronized with URL search parameters.
FE-STA-002.section: Deep Linking and Search Parameter State
FE-STA-002.evidence_quote: The URL is the most durable form of state in web applications. Search filters and pagination must be serialized into query parameters to ensure shareability.

TEST-E2E-001.title: Page Object Model (POM) for E2E Test Isolation
TEST-E2E-001.statement: Playwright end-to-end tests must encapsulate web page locators and user interactions within Page Object Model (POM) classes.
TEST-E2E-001.evidence_quote: Page Object Models reduce duplication and isolate test code from volatile UI structure. Tests interact with the page through meaningful business methods.

TEST-E2E-002.title: Automated E2E Verification of the Critical RAG Journey
TEST-E2E-002.statement: The CI quality gate must execute automated Playwright E2E tests verifying the core end-to-end journey: Login -> Document Upload -> Processing -> Chat Response with Citation.
TEST-E2E-002.evidence_quote: End-to-end testing must focus on high-value user journeys. Validating the core workflow from start to finish ensures critical business functionality remains operational.

FE-TS-001.title: Strict Zero-Any Policy in TypeScript
FE-TS-001.statement: The 'any' keyword is strictly prohibited in application code. Use unknown, generics, or explicit narrowing types.
FE-TS-001.section: Item 1: Understand the Relationship Between TypeScript and JavaScript
FE-TS-001.evidence_quote: The any type silences the type checker and your tooling. It undermines confidence in the system and hides bugs until runtime.

FE-TS-002.title: Discriminated Unions for Representing State
FE-TS-002.statement: Asynchronous UI states must be modeled using Discriminated Unions with a common literal discriminator property ('status') to make impossible states unrepresentable.
FE-TS-002.section: Item 28: Prefer Types That Always Represent Valid States
FE-TS-002.evidence_quote: Types that represent valid states make your code easier to write and reduce bugs. Discriminated unions make impossible states unrepresentable.

UI-A11Y-001.title: Semantic HTML and ARIA Labeling on Interactive Elements
UI-A11Y-001.statement: Interactive elements must use semantic HTML tags (<button>, <a>, <input>) and provide explicit aria-label attributes when icons lack text labels.
UI-A11Y-001.evidence_quote: Use native semantic HTML elements whenever possible. They provide built-in keyboard navigation and screen reader semantics that custom div containers lack.

UI-LAW-002.title: Fitts's Law: Minimum Target Size of 44x44px for Interactive Elements
UI-LAW-002.statement: Interactive touch and click targets (buttons, icon buttons, checkboxes) must have an effective hit area of at least 44x44 CSS pixels with adequate spacing.
UI-LAW-002.evidence_quote: The time to acquire a target is a function of the distance to and size of the target. Touch targets should be large enough (at least 44 × 44 pt) and have sufficient spacing.

UI-DLG-001.title: Focus Trapping and ESC Key Dismissal in Modal Dialogs
UI-DLG-001.statement: Modal dialogs must trap keyboard focus within the dialog container and dismiss immediately upon pressing the Escape key.
UI-DLG-001.evidence_quote: Modal dialogs require user interaction before returning to the parent window. Focus must be trapped inside the dialog, and Escape should provide a clean cancel.

UI-DLG-002.title: Explicit Two-Step Confirmation for Destructive Actions
UI-DLG-002.statement: Destructive operations (e.g. deleting knowledge bases, revoking keys) must require explicit confirmation with the resource name stated, and default focus must NOT rest on the destructive button.
UI-DLG-002.evidence_quote: For irreversible or destructive operations, require an explicit confirmation step. Clearly state what will be lost and never make the destructive action the default choice.

UI-GEN-001.title: Strict Prohibition of Emojis in Production Interface Elements
UI-GEN-001.statement: Emojis must not be used as interface icons, status badges, buttons, or navigation indicators in production interfaces.
UI-GEN-001.evidence_quote: System icons should be cohesive, vector-based, and specifically designed for the interface context. Do not rely on platform emojis for core interface feedback.

UI-LAW-001.title: Jakob's Law: Conform to Familiar User Interface Mental Models
UI-LAW-001.statement: Users spend most of their time on other sites; interface layouts, navigation patterns, and iconography must conform to familiar mental models rather than inventing proprietary navigation mechanics.
UI-LAW-001.evidence_quote: Users spend most of their time on other sites. This means that users prefer your site to work the same way as all the other sites they already know.

UI-LAW-003.title: Hick's Law: Minimize Options to Reduce Decision Latency
UI-LAW-003.statement: Break down complex choices into distinct progressive steps; menus and selection dialogs should limit initial choices to high-frequency actions.
UI-LAW-003.evidence_quote: The time it takes to make a decision increases with the number and complexity of choices. Simplify choices for the user by breaking complex tasks into smaller steps.

UI-LAW-004.title: Miller's Law: Chunk Complex Information into 5 to 9 Discrete Units
UI-LAW-004.statement: Complex interfaces and forms must organize related information into discrete visual chunks containing no more than 7 (+/- 2) elements per group.
UI-LAW-004.evidence_quote: The average person can only keep 7 (plus or minus 2) items in their working memory. Organize content into smaller chunks to help users process and memorize easily.

UI-PER-001.title: Perceived Performance via Skeleton Loaders (Doherty Threshold)
UI-PER-001.statement: Content areas with predictable structure must render layout-matching Skeleton Shimmer loaders instead of spinning loaders during data retrieval.
UI-PER-001.evidence_quote: Productivity soars when a computer and its users interact at a pace (<400ms) that ensures that neither has to wait on the other. Skeleton screens minimize perceived waiting time.

UI-STA-001.title: Mandatory Five-State Component Anatomy
UI-STA-001.statement: Every data-displaying component must explicitly implement all 5 UI states: Empty, Loading/Skeleton, Error (with retry), Success, and Interactive (Hover/Active/Disabled).
UI-STA-001.evidence_quote: Every asynchronous view must provide immediate, responsive visual feedback indicating system status, loading transitions, and actionable error conditions.

inmemory-vs-distributed-lock.verdict: In-memory promise mutexes are STRICTLY CONFINED to single-process test doubles (Mock/Fake repositories). Production services MUST enforce concurrency at the Database layer (SELECT FOR UPDATE) or Distributed Lock layer (Redis Redlock).
